slides.say: A wooden cube is painted on all six faces. Then it's cut into one hundred twenty-five identical small cubes, five along each edge. How many small cubes have paint on exactly one face?
I want to use this question to show you how we count in a painted cube. We don't count cube by cube. We ask, where is the small cube?
A small cube on a corner of the big cube touches three painted faces. So it has three painted faces.
at: A small cube on a corner

slides.say: A small cube on an edge, but not on a corner, touches two painted faces.
at: A small cube on an edge

slides.say: A small cube in the middle of a face touches only one painted face. That's the one we want.
at: in the middle of a face

slides: And a small cube inside the big cube isn't painted at all.

slides.say: So on each face, we take off the border. Each row has five cubes, and the border takes one at each end. Five minus two is three. So the middle of each face is three by three, nine cubes.
There are six faces, so six times nine, fifty-four. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: Let's check that everything adds up to one hundred twenty-five. A cube has eight corners, so eight small cubes have three painted faces.
at: Let's check that everything adds up

slides.say: A cube has twelve edges, and each edge has three small cubes between its corners. Twelve times three is thirty-six. These have two painted faces.
Thirty-six is choice number one, and it's a trap. It's the number with two painted faces, not one.
The inside is a cube three by three by three, twenty-seven. They have no paint. That's choice number three, another trap.
Eight plus thirty-six is forty-four. Plus fifty-four is ninety-eight. Plus twenty-seven is one hundred twenty-five. Everything fits.
And one hundred fifty, choice number four, is six times twenty-five, all the small painted squares, not the cubes. Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: choice number four, is six times
